# Depression in Children

**Authors:** Veeraraghavan Iyer, Yusra Azhar, Sunny P. Aslam

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Depressive disorders, as defined in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th ed. (DSM–5), include major depressive disorder (MDD), disruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD), persistent depressive disorder (PDD, also known as dysthymia), and unspecified depressive disorder. MDD remains the leading cause of disability among adolescents aged 10 to 19 (World Health Organization [WHO], 2014). Suicide is the third leading cause of death in this age group, with adolescent depression being a significant risk factor. Compared with matched controls, adolescents with depression report significantly more stressful life events in the year preceding the onset of symptoms.
